Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: The service-tunnel network is down. Nobody has run the wheels that power the shaft lifts in ten years. 'No travel,' says a Wrinkle's note on the hatch.
Suggested line: The service-tunnel network is down. The wheels that once turned the shaft lifts have spent ten years lighting the facade instead. 'No travel,' says a Wrinkle's note on the hatch.
Why: The current line says nobody runs the wheels, in a district built on wheels that never stop; this squares it and shows where the power went.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: A real recipe, written by hand, with a stain of actual sauce on the corner! A pinch of this, a spoonful of that. It is wonderfully imprecise. You tuck it away.
Suggested line: A real recipe, written by hand, with a stain of actual sauce on the corner! Flour: some. Salt: enough. Time: until it smells right. It is wonderfully imprecise. You tuck it away.
Why: Uses Chef Marlo's 'some' quantities so the card reads as his, with a sharper picture of the imprecision.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: The second wheel has been turning since before some of its runners were old enough to vote. A foreman's whistle hangs from a hook. You take it off its hook and put it in your pocket.
Suggested line: The second wheel has been turning since some of its runners were too small to reach the pedals. A foreman's whistle hangs from a hook. You pocket it.
Why: Drops 'old enough to vote' (odd in a monarchy) and the doubled hook; the image does the work.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: The third wheel's crew are children. Children! 'It is a school activity,' says a banner.
Suggested line: The third wheel's crew are children in school caps. 'It is a school activity,' says a banner. Nobody has rung the bell.
Why: Narration shows instead of exclaiming 'Children!'; the bell that never rings carries the horror quietly.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: You watch the neighbourhood carry Mr. Pell to his grave. A quiet tune accompanies the coffin as they lower it.
Suggested line: You watch the neighbourhood carry Mr. Pell to his grave. Nobody holds a permit to sing, so they sing very quietly. Nobody stops them.
Why: Replaces the vague 'a quiet tune accompanies' with one specific, sincere act of small defiance; no joke on the beat.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: The Beefcakes kept the kingdom's energy and its roads: the wheels, the mills, the throwers and the portal-rippers. {villain} put them all on wheels to light one small town. The rest of the kingdom went dark.
Suggested line: The Beefcakes kept the kingdom's energy and its roads: the wheels, the mills, the throwers and the portal-rippers. {villain} put them all on wheels to light one showpiece street. The rest of the kingdom went dark.
Why: 'One small town' in narration can read as the hub town; the facade is one showpiece street.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: A Showcase Quarter, built to show what the whole kingdom could be if everybody simply tried harder.
Suggested line: Every house in this quarter was built to show what the whole kingdom could be if everybody simply tried harder.
Why: The line spells the district name literally in a story file (token rule) and the sign need not repeat its own heading.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: To the Crease. The dead are not allowed down. The living are a little afraid of the dead down there. Be kind.
Suggested line: To the Crease. Living passengers only. The dead have asked to come down too; we are thinking about it. Be kind.
Why: The current sign contradicts itself (the dead are not allowed down, yet the living fear the dead down there); this is clear and funnier.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: The Paths tear where {villain} forced them into one shape. His hold is failing; the tears began the night someone escaped the Ministry.
Suggested line: The tears are temporary and fully under control. (Scrawled below: the Paths tear where {villain} forced them into one shape. His hold slipped the night someone escaped the Ministry.)
Why: An official sign would never admit his hold is failing; the fact survives as a Wrinkle's scrawl under the slogan, the Capital's core joke.

Speaker: Wren
Effective line: Back in one piece? Good. Mostly one piece.
Suggested line: Back in one piece? Good. Hesper charges by the piece.
Why: Wren's one sharp joke per scene, and a nod to Hesper's correction fee, instead of a repeated 'one piece'.

Speaker: Wren
Effective line: The records say he began as a good man. Keep that in mind. It does not excuse what he has done.
Suggested line: The records say he began well. His first decree put a hot lunch in front of every schoolchild. Remember that. It excuses nothing.
Why: The archivist is the natural voice for Primm's sincere early reforms; one concrete good deed makes him tragic before the castle.

Speaker: Widow Pell
Effective line: I talk to him in the parlour. I don't know what else to do. Please, if you can help.
Suggested line: I talk to him in the parlour. He was always the patient one. I'm not, it turns out. Please, if you can help.
Why: Gives Pell her own soft dry humour about herself, never at her loss, and keeps the plea.

Speaker: Captain Spotless
Effective line: I have measured eleven thousand visitors. I approved four. Nine thousand were sent home. The rest, I will not say.
Suggested line: I have measured twelve thousand visitors. I approved four. Nine thousand were sent home. The rest, I will not say.
Why: 'Eleven' is the prince's story clue; a gate tally should not spend it casually. Same joke, same shape.

Speaker: Capital guards and clerks
Effective line: Still above regulation. Still letting it go. Do not make me regret it.
Suggested line: Still one hair above regulation. I have thought about that hair all week. Do not make me regret it.
Why: Pays off his 'one hair' from the intro and shows a small human obsession instead of repeating 'still'.

Speaker: Rollo Spokes
Effective line: Here. From the old days: what we gave people who could keep going.
Suggested line: Here... from the old days. We gave these out... at the end of a shift. Remember ends?
Why: Breathless Rollo rhythm, a clearer reward line, and the quest's whole point (stopping) as the punchline.

Speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
Effective line: Everyone is so friendly! Everyone is so friendly. It is like living inside a greeting card.
Suggested line: Everyone is so friendly! Everyone is so friendly. It is like living inside a greeting card. The kind with nothing written in it.
Why: One more clause turns a flat simile into the slogan-and-whisper gap.

Speaker: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News
Effective line: Please continue to be happy, as scheduled! This has been your Deputy Minister of Good News!
Suggested line: Please continue to be happy, as scheduled! Lost Ministry property must be returned at once, and not spoken to!
Why: Puts the 'escaped Royal Asset' hunt into the broadcasts; 'not spoken to' is funny early and chilling after the reveal.

Speaker: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News
Effective line: Attention, citizens! Please remember: the exits are for ENTERING. The entrances are for EXITING.
Suggested line: Great news, citizens! The public records have never been tidier! Every untidy page has been corrected!
Why: The exit-is-the-entrance joke is already the exit guard's; this spends the broadcast on tidy records curdling into erased history, which sets up Wren.

Speaker: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News
Effective line: Anything else is an unapproved Direction.
Suggested line: If you remember things differently, please report to the Correction Ward. Your memory will be tidied too!
Why: Second box of the records broadcast: Plume's cheer over a real threat, pointing at a place the player can visit.

Speaker: Vivienne Quota, Minister of Efficiency
Effective line: You. Again. You cost me the Gainlands in four hours and eleven minutes. I have had the figure framed.
Suggested line: You. Again. You cost me the Gainlands in four hours and twelve minutes. I have had the figure framed.
Why: 'Eleven' is a story clue; Quota's precision works with any figure.

Speaker: Old Fern
Effective line: Granny Gristle needs hands on the compost rows down in the Dump. Peel from shell. Messy work.
Suggested line: Granny Gristle needs hands on the compost rows down in the Dump. Sorting peel from shell, all day. Messy. You'll hate it. Good.
Why: 'Peel from shell' reads as a typo; this is clear and gives Fern her grumbly last word over the tidy hare.

Speaker: Rollo Spokes
Effective line: Trained with... the Gainlands wheel crews. They told us... it was cardio.
Suggested line: Back in the Gainlands... we threw commuters. Now I'd pay... to be thrown.
Why: His other lines already say 'it was cardio'; this adds the Beefcakes' people-throwing transport and an exhausted joke.

Zone/Area: The Capital / The Old Service Tunnels
Speaker: (narration/UI)
Effective line: The junction crew trains on scrap: tyre flips, bin presses, dumbbells made of drain pipe. Every Garbage becomes muscle.
Suggested line: Beefcake bore, Gourmand vents, Necrocrat signs, Refusemancer drains. The junction crew lifts the scrap. Every Garbage becomes muscle.
Why: The Four-Faction Junction is the place to show the tunnels were built by all four Paths together; keeps the Garbage-to-muscle hint.

Speaker: Colonel Cornelius Crumb, Director of Culinary Defense
Effective line: HALT! This is a restricted pantry! Those recipes are confiscated for the war effort!
Suggested line: ATTENTION! This is a restricted pantry! Those recipes are confiscated for the war effort!
Why: HALT is Captain Spotless's catchphrase; Crumb barks drill-sergeant orders.
